bullet_feedback.bullet: Because the 270K+ row PostgreSQL workflow table had strict access limits, precomputed popular workflows into a category tree that the Claude skill searches first, with Redis caching full workflows to cut database queries
bullet_feedback.problem: Opens with a 20-word 'Because...' clause about table size and access limits, so the action ('precomputed popular workflows') arrives mid-line and the bullet ends on 'cut database queries' without telling me what the user of the tool gained.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: I could not restate why this mattered to a hiring manager without guessing; it reads as plumbing and I skipped it on the skim.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: what problem 'strict access limits' caused for the tool (slow, blocked, rate-limited?) and how this bullet relates to the 65% speedup in the bullet above
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Lead with what was built and for whom, then the constraint as a short reason; if it contributed to the 65% speedup, say so by merging or cross-referencing rather than adding a new number. e.g. 'Gave the Claude skill a fast first lookup: a precomputed category tree of popular workflows plus a Redis cache, since the 270K+ row PostgreSQL table had strict access limits'

bullet_feedback.bullet: Building capacity planning for Amazon Redshift maintenance like patching: Java logic that sets upper and lower bounds on reserved EC2 capacity to balance availability against cost, validated by backtesting
bullet_feedback.problem: The colon after 'patching' turns the second half into a noun phrase ('Java logic that sets...') rather than a sentence, and 'Building capacity planning' is vague as a verb phrase. It is the top bullet under the biggest brand but is the least AI/ML-related item on the page.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: The first bullet a recruiter reads sets the frame; here it says 'cloud capacity', not 'AI/ML', for an AI/ML target. The stitched phrasing also reads less like the candidate talking.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Rephrase as one sentence with a real verb ('Writing Java logic that sets...'); keep it short since it is a 2-month-in role. Ordering is chronological so leave it, but keep it to one tight line-and-a-half.

bullet_feedback.bullet: For a PhD-led robotics project aimed at ICLR, built a pipeline that overlays AnyGrasp’s candidate grasps on camera images in Open3D for a vision-language model, then tuned prompts so the model picks the right grasp more often
bullet_feedback.problem: Three unfamiliar names in a row ('AnyGrasp's candidate grasps', 'Open3D', 'vision-language model') before I know the goal, and the result 'more often' is unmeasured.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: This is one of the most ML-flavored roles on the page but it is the hardest to retell; 'more often' gives the reader nothing to repeat.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: whether any measured improvement in grasp selection exists; if not, keep it qualitative
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: State the goal in plain words first (helping a vision-language model choose where a robot arm should grab an object), then the method; drop 'in Open3D' to Skills if space is needed.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Reduced end-to-end latency 34% for a pipeline routing 6,000+ scraped research documents to inference by replacing S3 staging hops with Kinesis streams feeding Lambda
bullet_feedback.problem: 'S3 staging hops with Kinesis streams feeding Lambda' is three AWS service names in a row; a non-engineer only gets 'changed how data moves'. Fine for an engineer, but 'staging hops' is jargon.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: Minor: the 34% lands, but the reason it got faster is opaque to a recruiter.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Rephrase the method in plain words with the service names kept, e.g. 'by streaming documents through Kinesis to Lambda instead of writing each step to S3'.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Deployed a space-topic research tool for Amazon Leo’s public-policy team and set it up for handoff with AWS CDK infrastructure-as-code and GitHub Actions CI/CD, so Leo engineers new to the project now maintain it on AWS Fargate
bullet_feedback.problem: Five tooling names (AWS CDK, infrastructure-as-code, GitHub Actions, CI/CD, Fargate) carry most of the bullet; 'space-topic research tool' does not tell me what the tool does for the policy team.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: The real win (the client's own engineers took it over) is buried at the end behind a tool list.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: what the research tool does for the policy team, in a few words
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Say what the tool does, then the handoff outcome; keep one or two infrastructure names and let Skills carry the rest.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Built Redis caching in front of the Prisma ORM queries for Tortuga, the studio’s class scheduler with 20,000+ visits in its first 30 days, to reduce database load and latency
bullet_feedback.problem: 'the studio's' is unclear (TerpLabs is never called a studio), and 'to reduce database load and latency' is intent with no outcome; the 20,000+ number describes the app, not this work.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: A reader may credit the 20,000 visits to the caching work, or wonder what 'studio' refers to.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Introduce Tortuga first as the product ('Tortuga, TerpLabs' class scheduler with 20,000+ visits in its first 30 days'), then the caching; replace 'the studio's' with the company name.

page_feedback.problem: The AI/ML story is spread across five roles and starts with a non-ML AWS capacity bullet; there is no single place where 'LLM applications / ML infrastructure engineer' jumps out in the first 7 seconds.
page_feedback.why_it_matters: On a skim I came away with 'cloud/backend person who uses LLMs', not 'ML infrastructure engineer'. The Bedrock retraining loop - the most ML-infra item - sits in the middle of the page.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: Keep chronological order but make the first bullet of each role its most AI-relevant one; within the Amazon Leo role the retraining bullet is already first, which is good.

page_feedback.problem: 'Amazon Leo' and 'UMD App Development Contracting' are unexplained; a recruiter may not know Amazon Leo is an Amazon program, so the client brand does not land.
page_feedback.why_it_matters: This is the role with the most ML-infra evidence, and the header is the most confusing one on the page.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: Clarify in a few words what Amazon Leo is (e.g. a parenthetical on first mention) without adding new scope.

page_feedback.problem: Several bullets use stacked tech names as the main content ('React and TypeScript Electron app with a visual React Flow editor and Jest-tested validation'; 'AWS CDK infrastructure-as-code and GitHub Actions CI/CD').
page_feedback.why_it_matters: These phrases are hard to say out loud and push human_voice and plain_language down; the Skills section already lists the tools.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: Keep the one tool that explains the design choice in each bullet and leave the rest to Skills.

page_feedback.problem: Bold is used only on numbers (65%, 90%, 34%, 93%, 50.9M) but not on the IEX 99,122 of 99,123 result, which is the most memorable number on the page.
page_feedback.why_it_matters: Bold drives the eye on a skim; the strongest proof point is unbolded while 50.9M (a volume, not a result) is bolded.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: Consider moving the bold from '50.9M' to '99,122 of 99,123 fills'.
